content: Programs should highlight the importance of receiving the influenza vaccine and provide detailed guidance on how, where, and when individuals can obtain it. Clinics and other healthcare providers catering to travelers should review the indications for influenza vaccination prior to travel and offer the vaccine if deemed appropriate. This is particularly relevant for foreign travelers. Healthcare facility administrators must ensure that influenza vaccines are made available to all personnel before the onset of the influenza season. Staff should be provided with comprehensive educational materials about the vaccine and strongly encouraged to receive it. This includes personnel working in intensive care units, medical/surgical units, nursing homes, and chronic-care facilities. To improve vaccination compliance, strategies such as using mobile carts to deliver vaccines directly to hospital wards or other work sites, and offering vaccines during night and weekend shifts, should be implemented. Additionally, follow-up campaigns early in the course of a community outbreak may further enhance compliance. Information regarding influenza surveillance can be accessed through the CDC Voice Information System (Influenza Update) by calling (404) 332-4551 or via the CDC Information Service on the Public Health Network electronic bulletin board. From October through May, this information is updated at least biweekly. Periodic updates on influenza are also published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR). State and local health departments should be consulted for information on vaccine availability, access to vaccination programs, and details about state or local influenza activity. The U.S. Government Printing Office in Washington, DC, can also provide relevant information and can be reached at (202) 783-3238. The data in the weekly MMWR are provisional and based on weekly reports submitted to the CDC by state health departments. The reporting week concludes at the close of business on Friday, and the compiled national data are officially released to the public the following Friday. Inquiries about the MMWR Series, including materials for potential publication, should be directed to the Editor, MMWR Series, Mailstop C-08, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, GA 30333, or by calling (404) 332-4555. All materials in the MMWR Series are in the public domain and may be used or reprinted without special permission, though proper citation of the source is appreciated. For further reference, see the U.S. Government Printing Office publication: 1994-533-178/05006 Region IV. Additionally, the study by Lui KJ and Kendal AP, titled Impact of influenza epidemics on mortality in the United States from October 1972 to May 1985, published in the American Journal of Public Health in 1987 (77:712-6), provides valuable insights.
